paragraphs.title: Opening: Vanity and the Lack of Profit

answers: As the son of David and king in Jerusalem
As a priest in the wilderness
As a ruler in Egypt
easy.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:1 calls him “the son of David, king in Jerusalem.”
easy.q: How is the Preacher introduced in the opening verse?

answers: Everything is new
All is vanity
Everything lasts forever
easy.explanation: The Preacher says, “Vanity of vanities... all is vanity.”
easy.q: What is the Preacher’s central declaration in the opening?

answers: What causes the sun to rise?
How many generations will come?
What profit a man has from all his labour
easy.explanation: He asks what profit a man has from all his labour under the sun.
easy.q: What question does the Preacher ask in verse 3?

answers: If everything passes away, what lasting profit comes from labour?
If everything is vanity, no one must work
If everything is vanity, every achievement becomes greater
medium.explanation: The statement about vanity leads to the question of what remains from human labour.
medium.q: How does the declaration that all is vanity relate to the question about human labour?

answers: A lasting gain or benefit
A high place on a mountain
A memory of an ancient person
medium.explanation: In this context, “profit” means gain or benefit that remains from labour.
medium.q: What does “profit” mean in the question, “What profit hath a man”?

answers: Above the heavens
Under the sun
Within the sea
medium.explanation: The verse asks about labour that a man takes “under the sun.”
medium.q: Where does the Preacher place the question about human labour?

answers: A person works, but it is unclear what lasting result remains
A person does not work and therefore cannot succeed
A person knows that all labour remains forever
challenge.explanation: The verses set human labour against the possibility that it produces no lasting profit.
challenge.q: What central tension appears in the first three verses?

answers: That there is only a small amount of vanity
That vanity is emphasized in the strongest terms
That vanity applies only to the king
challenge.explanation: The repeated phrase intensifies the declaration that all is vanity.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “Vanity of vanities” emphasize?

answers: That they will leave a permanent mark
That they will be done under the sun
That they will require labour
challenge.explanation: The opening raises doubt that human achievements will leave an enduring mark.
challenge.q: What lasting benefit is not guaranteed for human achievements?

paragraphs.title: The Cycles of Nature and the Absence of Newness

answers: One generation passeth away, and another cometh
All generations remain together
There are no more generations
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh.”
easy.q: What happens from one generation to another?

answers: Toward the mountains
Into the desert
Into the sea
easy.explanation: The passage says, “All the rivers run into the sea.”
easy.q: Where do all the rivers run?

answers: It is always truly new
It has already existed in former times
It will remain forever
easy.explanation: The passage says that what appears new “hath been already of old time.”
easy.q: What does the passage say about something that seems new?

answers: Cycles and repeated movement
Complete stillness
One-time, sudden change
medium.explanation: Each natural example moves repeatedly through an established circuit.
medium.q: What do the sun, wind, and rivers demonstrate together?

answers: The eye is unable to see anything
The eye is never fully satisfied with what it sees
The eye quickly falls asleep
medium.explanation: The phrase describes an unfulfilled desire to see more and more.
medium.q: What does “the eye is not satisfied with seeing” mean?

answers: The same patterns and courses are repeated
Nature disappears completely
Human beings control all of nature
medium.explanation: The repeated movements present the world as operating in familiar cycles.
medium.q: How does nature’s repetition support the idea that there is no newness?

answers: Generations pass away, and people are forgotten
Every generation remembers everyone
Generations never change
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the passing of generations with the lack of remembrance of former things.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between changing generations and remembrance?

answers: The sea is not full
The rivers return to the place from which they came
The waters do not move
challenge.explanation: The rivers return to their starting place and then flow again.
challenge.q: Which detail most strongly reinforces the repeated cycle of the waters?

answers: There is much movement, but little newness and remembrance
Everything advances toward a completely new goal
Only nature repeats, while people are always remembered
challenge.explanation: Nature repeats its cycles, while people and their works eventually pass from remembrance.
challenge.q: What conclusion arises from both nature and human history?

answers: The Preacher
A future generation
The rivers
easy.explanation: The Preacher identifies himself as the one who was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
easy.q: Who says, “I the Preacher was king over Israel”?

answers: Ignore it
Seek and search it out by wisdom
Change its course
easy.explanation: He gave his heart to seek and search out all things done under heaven.
easy.q: What did the Preacher determine to do concerning what is done under heaven?

answers: As complete and perfect
As vanity and vexation of spirit
As entirely new
easy.explanation: He says, “all is vanity and vexation of spirit.”
easy.q: How does the Preacher describe the result of his investigation?

answers: His position allows him to describe a broad investigation of what is done
His position prevents him from seeing the world
His position limits him to studying nature
medium.explanation: After identifying himself as king, he describes searching out all things done under heaven.
medium.q: How does the Preacher’s position relate to the scope of his investigation?

answers: Chasing after something that cannot be grasped
Great joy over an achievement
Rest after labour
medium.explanation: The expression pictures a futile pursuit, like trying to catch the wind.
medium.q: What does “vexation of spirit” mean in this passage?

answers: His investigation of all things done under heaven
The complete absence of human activity
His desire to avoid wisdom
medium.explanation: After examining what is done under heaven, he calls it a sore travail.
medium.q: What leads the Preacher to describe human activity as a sore travail?

answers: Some wrongs cannot be corrected by investigation alone
Every problem is solved through knowledge
There is no deficiency in the world
challenge.explanation: The verse acknowledges that some crooked things cannot be made straight.
challenge.q: What does “That which is crooked cannot be made straight” mean in the context of investigation?

answers: Every deficiency can be counted
Deficiencies are too extensive or numerous to measure
There are no deficiencies in reality
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the extent of what is lacking by saying it cannot be numbered.
challenge.q: What does “that which is wanting cannot be numbered” suggest?

answers: Reality is futile and contains defects that cannot be corrected
Reality is perfect but difficult to understand
Reality changes only because of the seasons
challenge.explanation: The Preacher describes both the futility of human activity and the uncorrected flaws in the world.
challenge.q: How are “vanity” and “crookedness” connected in the Preacher’s description?

answers: He had gained very little
He had become great and gained more wisdom
He had never learned wisdom
easy.explanation: He says, “I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom.”
easy.q: What does the Preacher say about the wisdom he had gained?

answers: Madness and folly
The seasons of the year
The boundaries of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: He gave his heart to know wisdom and also madness and folly.
easy.q: What did the Preacher examine besides wisdom?

answers: Grief and sorrow
Joy and peace
Remembrance and newness
easy.explanation: The final verse says, “in much wisdom is much grief” and increased knowledge brings increased sorrow.
easy.q: What increases as wisdom and knowledge increase?

answers: To investigate contrasting kinds of thought and conduct
To prove that folly alone is valuable
To stop thinking about reality
medium.explanation: His investigation included both wisdom and folly as contrasting aspects of human experience.
medium.q: Why did the Preacher examine both wisdom and folly?

answers: Lack of good judgment or foolishness
Deep remembrance
Difficult labour
medium.explanation: Folly means foolishness or a lack of wisdom.
medium.q: What does “folly” mean in this passage?

answers: More wisdom and knowledge bring more grief and sorrow
More wisdom removes all pain
More folly brings greater remembrance
medium.explanation: The verse directly connects increased wisdom and knowledge with increased grief and sorrow.
medium.q: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in the final verse?

answers: This also is vexation of spirit
Wisdom solves every crooked thing
Folly is better than wisdom
challenge.explanation: He concludes that examining wisdom and folly is also “vexation of spirit.”
challenge.q: What conclusion does the Preacher draw from his study of wisdom and folly?

answers: Wisdom guarantees a life without pain
Wisdom can increase awareness and therefore increase sorrow
Wisdom has no connection with pain
challenge.explanation: The passage states that increasing knowledge brings increasing sorrow.
challenge.q: What relationship between wisdom and pain is suggested by the passage?

answers: Even wisdom offers no complete profit and may bring grief
Wisdom is the one form of newness that never repeats
Wisdom guarantees that a person will be remembered forever
challenge.explanation: The ending shows both the limits of wisdom and the sorrow that may accompany greater understanding.
challenge.q: How does the ending of the chapter support its main idea?
